notes: Historical periods use PepsiCo fiscal years ended Dec 30, 2023; Dec 28, 2024; and Dec 27, 2025 as shown in PepsiCo’s FY2025 Form 10-K. ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-form-10k.pdf))

EBIT is modeled as GAAP Operating Profit from the consolidated statement of income (includes impairment of intangible assets in GAAP operating profit). ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-form-10k.pdf))

D&A comes from the cash flow line item “Depreciation and amortization.” Capital expenditures come from the cash flow line item “Capital spending” converted to an absolute positive value (cash outflow in the filing). ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-form-10k.pdf))

NWC calculation (for historical and as the driver for forecast %): (Total Current Assets - Cash and cash equivalents - Short-term investments) - (Total Current Liabilities - Short-term debt obligations). Negative NWC implies supplier/vendor financing and reduces modeled reinvestment needs. ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-form-10k.pdf))

Tax rate is the historical effective tax rate computed from GAAP provision for income taxes / income before income taxes (3-year average). ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-form-10k.pdf))

NOL balance is approximated from the 10-K note stating operating loss carryforwards and income tax credits totaling $35.5 billion as of Dec 27, 2025; NOL utilization % is not separately disclosed, so it is set to null. ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-form-10k.pdf))

2026-2030 revenue growth is a base-case conversion of management’s 2026 organic guidance (constant-currency, excludes FX/acquisitions/divestitures) into reported net revenue growth; future FX and acquisition impacts are not explicitly modeled and are embedded in the growth path. ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-prepared-management-remarks.pdf))

catalysts: Outperformance of the 2026 organic revenue guide (toward the high end of the 2 to 4 percent range), indicating stronger volume/repricing/mix execution. ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-prepared-management-remarks.pdf))

Sustained productivity savings and cost/mix actions that keep operating margin expansion on track versus management’s 2026 expectations. ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-prepared-management-remarks.pdf))

Portfolio reshaping and innovation execution (brand restaging and product pipeline) improving shelf presence and unit economics over multiple quarters. ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-prepared-management-remarks.pdf))
company_overview: PepsiCo is a leading global beverage and convenient food company with brands including Lay’s, Doritos, Cheetos, Gatorade, Pepsi-Cola, Mountain Dew, Quaker and SodaStream. ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-form-10k.pdf))

PepsiCo is organized into six reportable segments spanning PepsiCo Foods North America, PepsiCo Beverages North America, International Beverages Franchise (incl. SodaStream), EMEA, Latin America Foods, and Asia Pacific Foods. ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-form-10k.pdf))

Through operations, authorized bottlers, contract manufacturers, and other third parties, PepsiCo makes, markets, distributes and sells beverages and convenient foods serving customers in more than 200 countries and territories. ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-form-10k.pdf))

In many geographies, The Coca-Cola Company is PepsiCo’s primary beverage competitor. ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-form-10k.pdf))
current_context: Management expects full-year 2026 organic revenue to increase between 2 and 4 percent, aiming to deliver the high end during 2H 2026. ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-prepared-management-remarks.pdf))

Core operating margin is expected to increase in 2026 as productivity savings and benefits of net revenue growth offset planned incremental advertising/marketing and operating expense inflation. ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-prepared-management-remarks.pdf))

Core constant-currency EPS is expected to increase 4 to 6 percent, with core EPS growth approximately 5 to 7 percent on a reported basis (per management commentary). ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-prepared-management-remarks.pdf))
investment_highlights: Base case assumes modest, steady net revenue growth translating management’s 2026 organic outlook into reported net revenue growth and then fading to mature growth rates through 2030.

EBIT margin recovers gradually from FY2025 GAAP operating profit margin toward a normalized terminal level, reflecting continued productivity savings and commercial/brand investment discipline. ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-form-10k.pdf))
D&A and capex intensity are anchored to recent historical ratios to reflect a mature capital framework rather than aggressive step-ups in reinvestment.

Working capital remains a cash contributor in the model given negative NWC derived from balance-sheet current assets/liabilities (cash and short-term investments excluded; short-term debt excluded). ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-form-10k.pdf))
key_risks: Tariffs and input/transportation/packaging cost inflation could pressure operating margins and cash generation. ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-prepared-management-remarks.pdf))
FX translation and demand softness may reduce reported net revenue growth versus the base-case path.
Large GAAP impairments or other restructuring-related charges could distort operating profit and recurring cash flow assumptions.

valuation_summary: DCF uses a tax-rate and WACC calibrated to a mature consumer staples profile, with terminal value based on Gordon growth (terminal growth 2.5%).

Forecast drivers are constrained by historical operating intensity (EBIT margin, D&A and capex % of sales) plus management’s 2026 directional guidance for organic revenue and margin improvement. ([investors.pepsico.com](https://investors.pepsico.com/docs/pepsico-5v9wci20/media/Files/investors/q4-2025-prepared-management-remarks.pdf))
Comps serve as a reasonableness check using peer EV/EBITDA, EV/Sales, and forward P/E from Finviz for a quick valuation cross-check. ([finviz.com](https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=KO))
